rationale: Large cohort reviews and segregation analyses demonstrate that monoallelic carriers of biallelic/recessive NOTCH3 loss-of-function variants are predominantly asymptomatic or display only incidental non-specific headaches, supporting a distinct autosomal recessive inheritance mode compared to classic CADASIL. However, the literature also documents notable counter-examples where heterozygous carriers of null/loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants developed premature and recurrent ischemic strokes in early adulthood (e.g., stroke onset at 28 and 39 years), as well as subclinical vascular degeneration overlapping with CADASIL pathology, indicating variable penetrance or potential susceptibility to cerebrovascular disease in some heterozygous carriers.

evidence.text: A comprehensive analysis of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants (26 with loss-of-function and 24 with cysteine-involving variants) confirmed that monoallelic carriers of loss-of-function variants are predominantly asymptomatic, with only a few cases reporting nonspecific headaches, supporting an autosomal recessive loss-of-function disease mechanism distinct from classical dominant CADASIL.

evidence.text: Segregation analysis in a family with early-onset leukoencephalopathy caused by a homozygous null variant (c.2984delC) showed that consanguineous heterozygous parents were clinically unaffected, and three unrelated individuals harbored heterozygous NOTCH3 null variants as incidental findings, reinforcing recessive inheritance.

source.quote: The consanguineous parents were confirmed as heterozygous variant carriers. In addition, three heterozygous NOTCH3 null variants were reported as incidental findings in three unrelated cases analyzed in our center.

evidence.text: Evaluation of parents heterozygous for the homozygous NOTCH3 null mutation p.C966* revealed vascular smooth muscle degeneration and decreased expression of NOTCH3 and its downstream targets in arterial vessels similar to CADASIL, albeit less severe, indicating subclinical vascular pathology in heterozygous carriers.

source.title: Homozygous NOTCH3 null mutation and impaired NOTCH3 signaling in recessive early‐onset arteriopathy and cavitating leukoencephalopathy
source.quote: The heterozygous parents displayed similar but less dramatic trends in decrease in the expression of NOTCH3 and its targets, as well as in vessel degeneration. This study suggests a functional link between NOTCH3 deficiency and pathogenesis of vascular leukoencephalopathies.

evidence.text: Three pediatric patients with biallelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 loss-of-function variants presented between 9 and 14 months of age with developmental delay, seizures, and vascular leukoencephalopathy, whereas their heterozygous carrier parents did not display early childhood-onset disease.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: The patients presented at 9 to 14 months of age with developmental delay, seizures, or both.

conflicts: While systematic cohorts find that monoallelic carriers of NOTCH3 loss-of-function variants are predominantly asymptomatic or present solely with nonspecific headaches, individual reports document premature stroke (ages 28 and 39) in heterozygous null carriers.

Histopathological and molecular evaluations in heterozygous parents of null-variant probands show smooth muscle degeneration and decreased NOTCH3 expression in cerebral vessels, disputing the view that monoallelic status confers zero vascular phenotypic change.

new_directions.question_text: What is the lifetime penetrance of stroke and vascular white matter lesions in heterozygous carriers of NOTCH3 loss-of-function variants compared to age-matched controls?
new_directions.rationale: Conflicting findings exist between large series reporting asymptomatic carrier parents and individual pedigree reports documenting strokes at ages 28 and 39 years, requiring systematic prospective neuroimaging and clinical registries.

new_directions.question_text: Do hypomorphic vs. complete null NOTCH3 alleles exert haploinsufficiency effects that modify conventional cardiovascular and cerebrovascular risk factors?
new_directions.rationale: Pippucci et al. demonstrated decreased arterial smooth muscle NOTCH3 downstream signaling and subclinical vascular degeneration in heterozygous parents, suggesting a potential gene-environment or modifier effect that could trigger stroke under vascular stress.
